references.text: Earlier in the chapter it is mentioned that the Levite lived in the hill country of Ephraim, confirming his origin from this area.
Another Levite from Bethlehem in Judah who traveled to the hill country of Ephraim shows a similar travel pattern.
Describes the house of the Lord in Shiloh, which is likely the place the Levite referred to when he mentioned the house of the Lord.
The tabernacle of the Lord is mentioned as a holy place, relevant to the Levite's journey to the house of the Lord.
Mentions the house of the Lord in Shiloh where Israelites came to worship, the same destination the Levite mentioned.
Bethlehem in Judah is mentioned as his hometown, showing a geographical connection to the same city.
Describes how no one took them in, explaining the Levite's complaint that no one would give them lodging.
